sections.preface: Planar graph duality, anchored by Euler's formula and Whitney's matroid criterion, generalizes to simplicial complexes via dimension-reversal and boundary/coboundary operators.
Dart permutations and double-coset constructions yield a universal algebraic representation of graphs and maps, extending Sabidussi's coset-graph theory.

sections.section_name: Singularities, Vanishing Cycles, and ADE Diagrams
sections.preface: Catastrophe theory and Picard-Lefschetz vanishing cycles link singularities to monodromy, producing ADE Dynkin graphs, McKay correspondences, and quivers.

sections.section_name: Gromov Hyperbolicity and Tree-Like Metric Spaces
sections.preface: Gromov's delta-hyperbolicity formalizes tree-likeness in metric spaces and graphs through thin geodesic triangles and the four-point condition.

sections.section_name: Whitney Stratification and Group-Action Orbit Types
sections.preface: Whitney stratification decomposes singular spaces into compatible smooth strata, and group actions on geometric realizations refine this with orbit-type strata and quotient singularities.
Mutual information, the data processing inequality, rate-distortion theory, and domain-adaptation bounds certify that geometric abstractions preserve task-relevant information across domains.

sections.section_name: Bit Budgets, IDF Weighting, and Scaling Laws
sections.preface: Singularity-IDF weighting, Pythagorean feature decompositions, partition functions, and bit-budget scaling laws together quantify the complexity of stratified agent representations.
